blocks.text: During a chemical reaction, reactants are converted into products. So, the concentration of the products increases with the corresponding decrease in the concentration of the reactants as they are being consumed.

blocks.title: Rate of reaction
blocks.text: The rate of a reaction is defined as the change in the concentration of a reactant or a product divided by the time taken for the change.

blocks.alt: Graph with axes O-Y (an upward arrow beside it) and O-X (Time). For A to B, the curve 'Concentration of reactant "A"' falls steeply from a high value at the start and flattens towards the time axis; the curve 'Concentration of product "B"' rises steeply from zero and flattens. Both curves carry plotted points and cross early in the reaction.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.1: Change in the concentration of reactants and products with time for the reaction A to B (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.1).

blocks.latex: \text{Rate of reaction} = \frac{\text{change in concentration of the substance}}{\text{time taken for the change}}
blocks.text_alt: Rate of reaction = change in concentration of the substance / time taken for the change

blocks.text: Where Δx is a very small change in the concentration of a reactant or a product in a very small time interval Δt.
The situation is explained graphically in Figure 7.1. for the reactant A which is changing irreversibly to the product B.

The slope of the graph for the reactant or the product is steepest at the beginning. This shows a rapid decrease in the concentration of the reactant and consequently, a rapid increase in the concentration of the product. As the reaction proceeds, the slope becomes less steep indicating that the reaction is slowing down with time, ultimately both the curves become parallel. It means that the rate of a reaction is changing every moment. This is the stage of completion of reaction.
The rate of reaction has the units of concentration divided by time. Usually, the concentration is expressed in mol dm⁻³ and the time in second, thus the units for the reaction rate are mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

blocks.text_alt: Rate of reaction = mol dm⁻³ / seconds = mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹

blocks.text: However, for a slow reaction the units may be mol dm⁻³ min⁻¹ or even mol dm⁻³ h⁻¹. For a gas phase reaction, units of pressure are used in the place of molar concentrations.

The rate of a general reaction, A → B, can be expressed in terms of rate of disappearance of the reactant A or the rate of appearance of the product B mathematically, where [A] and [B] are the concentrations of A and B, respectively.

The negative sign with  indicates a decrease in the concentration of the reactant A. Since the concentration of product increases with time, the sign in rate expression involving the change of concentration of product is positive.
